newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus approves Kirch TV stake swap.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus approves Kirch TV stake swap.

text.p: French pay television group Canal Plus said on Wednesday its board had approved a stake swap with German media mogul Leo Kirch.
It said a deal would be finalised in the next few days after which details would be published.

The statement said the supervisory board had at its meeting allowed management to sell the company's 37.5 percent stake in German pay-television company Premiere to the Kirch group while allowing the acquisition from Kirch of 45 percent in Italy's Telepiu.

Premiere is currently owned by Canal Plus, Kirch and Bertelsmann. The sale of the stake by Canal Plus would allow the French group to leave the German market while the two German companies -- which only a year ago were bitter rivals working on separate plans to launch digital satellite television services -- can control the pay televison service.
Canal Plus already owns a 45 percent stake in Telepiu following its merger with Nethold.
Analysts had estimated the value of Canal Plus' Premiere stake at between 1.7 billion and 2.4 billion francs, and Kirch's Telepiu stake at between 1.3 billion and 1.4 billion francs.
They expect Canal Plus to get a cash payment of around 900 million francs.
The deal had been expected for months and Canal Plus shares rallied for the past week, adding 1.33 percent to 1,223 francs at 1357 GMT.
